title: comfy.yaml
description: Human-authored manifest. Declares what a workspace should contain; comfy-lock.yaml records how it resolved.

name.description: Capability name. Groups the files that must be installed together.

source.description: hf:<owner>/<repo>, gh:<owner>/<repo>@<tag>, civitai:<modelVersionId>, or a direct URL.

file.description: Path within the source repo. Omit for sources that name a single file.

revision.description: Moving ref the lock pins to a commit.

as.description: Local filename, if it should differ from upstream's.

type.description: Model type: lora, vae, checkpoint, diffusion_model, ...

sha256.description: REQUIRED for a direct-URL source: nothing about a bare URL can be resolved from headers, so the hash must be stated. Ignored for hf:/civitai: sources, which resolve it.

then.$comment: A civitai source's filename comes from the API, so it is not knowable offline. `as` makes the install path derivable from the manifest alone, which is what lets check-lock.sh run without network.

^x-.description: Consumer extension. `additionalProperties: false` is what makes `instal:` an error instead of a silent no-op, so extensions have to be NAMED rather than allowed by relaxing it -- the convention OpenAPI settled on. comfyfetch ignores these; they exist so a consumer can carry its own metadata (trigger words, family generation, packaging) in the file it already maintains.

Consumer extension. `additionalProperties: false` is what makes `instal:` an error instead of a silent no-op, so extensions have to be NAMED rather than allowed by relaxing it -- the convention OpenAPI settled on. comfyfetch ignores these; they exist so a consumer can carry its own metadata (trigger words, family generation, packaging) in the file it already maintains.

auth.description: Host -> environment variable holding that host's credential. The CLI resolves a source's credential by the URL's host, so no per-model annotation is needed.

additionalProperties.description: MUST be an ${ENV_VAR} reference. A literal is rejected by the schema so a token cannot be committed by accident.

profiles.description: Named sets of capabilities to resolve together. A member is either a model's `name` or another profile's name, so profiles compose by set union -- which is the composition case ("sometimes I want both") without inheritance, overrides, or diamonds.

capabilities.description: Named capabilities: which profiles provide them, and which model TYPES a graph needs to actually render. Absent from this schema until now, which meant it passed by accident rather than by validation -- the top level simply was not closed.

profiles.description: PLURAL and load-bearing: an add-on profile resolves no checkpoint by design, so a capability's contract is checked against the UNION of the profiles it names.

requires.description: Model `type:` values a graph needs. A capability requiring `vae` that resolves zero is a graph that loads and cannot render.
